title: Rapid Hydration Profiles and Graceful Slice Loading
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: Cold starts when moving a tenant onto dedicated capacity create long tail latencies and increased p99s due to full-weight loads and cold KV caches. Current prewarm strategies focus on whole-model prefetch or tenant-wide warm pools which either waste memory or are slow to scale. Proposal: introduce per-tenant hydration profiles and a 'graceful slice loading' runtime to reduce cold-start time and cost. Hydration profiles encode which model components (tokenizers, embedding matrices, key/value projection layers, attention kernels) must be loaded first for a given SLO tier and workload type. Graceful slice loading allows a node to serve traffic with a minimal fast-path subset of weights (quantized or distilled slices) and then progressively backfill full precision weights and KV cache in the background, prioritizing hot parameter slices and KV prefixes. The feature should integrate with autoscaling admission controls so we only admit requests to partially hydrated nodes when latency budgets allow. This ticket covers design and implementation of the profile schema, runtime admission gating, prioritized slice loader, and KV prefill controller for the dedicated fleet runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start median time-to-first-token (TTFT) for small-to-medium models reduced from baseline by >= 60% in lab tests (baseline measured on existing dedicated fleet).
p95 cold-start latency reduced by >= 40% without increasing steady-state per-token cost by more than 5% for representative workloads.
Hydration profile schema defined, documented, and versioned in the model registry; profile selection works for tenant, model, and route-level overrides.
Runtime can serve traffic from nodes with partial slice residency and transparently complete responses as full slices become available (no client-visible errors or inconsistent logits).
Automated e2e test harness exercising admission gating, slice backfill, and KV prefill is added to CI and green.
Monitoring dashboards for TTFT, slice-load-duration, KV-prefill-rate, admission-deny-rate, and cost delta are live in Console (links in 'links').
implementation_plan: Design: finalize hydration profile fields (priority groups, min_slices_to_serve, preferred_quantization_levels, kv_prefix_priority) and store in model registry.
Runtime: implement a slice loader that accepts ordered slice manifests and atomically advances a node's serveable-residency pointer; support background upgrade to higher precision.
Admission controller: extend fleet admission to check a node's current residency against request SLO and either route, queue (with SLA-aware timeout), or fallback to other capacity tiers.
KV prefill controller: implement tenant-scoped prefix hydrator that uses recent trace telemetry to backfill the most likely KV prefixes first and seeds short-lived caches for load bursts.
Fallback & safety: on failure to backfill in time, ensure deterministic graceful degradation to lower-fidelity fast-path with confidence calibration to avoid hallucination spikes.
API/metrics: add slice-level telemetry, labels for hydration profiles, and expose per-tenant warm-status in the Console API.
Tests: unit tests for slice loader, integration tests simulating progressive hydration, and canary runs on a shadow fleet before customer traffic.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Lab validation: run synthetic load against dedicated test fleet with varied model sizes (7B/13B/70B) and collect TTFT & p95 metrics.
Phase 1 - Internal canary: enable on 5% of internal tenants with noncritical traffic; verify metrics and cost impact over 2 weeks.
Phase 2 - Controlled customer pilot: onboard 2 customers (opt-in) on dedicated nodes; collect customer SRE feedback and iterate.
Phase 3 - Gradual ramp: enable hydration profiles by default on new dedicated pools and provide opt-out & profile overrides in Console.
Rollback: traffic will be shifted to fully-hydrated nodes and admission gating disabled if p95 or error rate regressions exceed thresholds for 30 minutes.
Post-launch: evaluate savings and whether to promote profiles to autoscale policies as a cost-control lever.
metrics_and_targets: Median TTFT (cold-start): target <= 4s for 7B, <= 8s for 13B at test conditions
p95 cold-start latency: reduce by >= 40% vs baseline
Slice load throughput: ability to load prioritized slice within 200ms for top-1 priority group
KV-prefill hit-rate during first 60s of tenant traffic: >= 70% for profiled prefixes
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Partial-residency serving could produce subtle quality regressions. Mitigation: confidence calibration layer and automatic quality checks comparing logits produced by fast-path vs fully-loaded path during canary runs.

Risk: Increased complexity in admission logic could cause routing oscillations. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, hysteresis on decisions, and a runtime health-check that reverts to fully-hydrated routing on instability.

Risk: KV-prefill could waste bandwidth and cost if heuristics are wrong. Mitigation: throttle background backfill, use short TTLs for prefetched entries, and monitor prefill hit-rate; provide opt-out at tenant level.

Risk: Interactions with autoscaler causing thrashing (scale up/down rapidly). Mitigation: integrate hydration state into autoscaler signals and add a cost-aware cool-down window for nodes undergoing hydration.
